title.justification: The title of the paper is explicitly stated in the document as 'Neural computations in prosopagnosia.' This is indicated clearly at the beginning of the document.

extractions.description: This paper investigates the neural computations related to face identification abilities, particularly focusing on a case of acquired pure prosopagnosia (patient PS). The study uses EEG, RSA, and deep neural networks to analyze and model brain activity in response to visual stimuli, aiming to uncover deficits in high-level visual and semantic neural computations associated with face recognition in prosopagnosic patients.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The focus of the paper is on neural computations related to face recognition, particularly in individuals with prosopagnosia. The research is primarily concerned with cognitive neuroscience and neural processing, rather than climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We aimed to identify neural computations underlying the loss of face identification ability by modelling the brain activity of brain-lesioned patient PS, a well-documented case of acquired pure prosopagnosia.

primary_category.justification: The core theme of the paper revolves around understanding neural mechanisms involved in face recognition impairments in prosopagnosia, which is not related to any Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development goals.
primary_category.quote: The human brain is equipped with sophisticated machinery optimised to quickly and effectively recognise faces... A dramatic contrast to this typically efficient process has been revealed in brain-lesioned patients with an inability to recognise faces, individuals called acquired prosopagnosics.

secondary_categories.justification: Similar to the primary category, there is no secondary focus on Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development as the research centers on neural and cognitive aspects of prosopagnosia.
secondary_categories.quote: Findings from these patients have refined the functional role and the distributed nature of the face-sensitive brain regions in the ventral stream.

primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category classification follows the primary category, focusing on neuroscience rather than environmental or sustainable themes.
primary_sub_category.quote: We used Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA) to correlate human EEG representations with those of deep neural network (DNN) models...

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no secondary sustainable development sub-categories applicable here, as the entire focus of the research is on neural processing and cognitive science.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Neural decoding shows abnormal neural evidence for face individuation in PS.

applications.value: Investigation of neural computations in prosopagnosia
applications.justification: The primary application highlighted in the paper is the advanced understanding of neural dynamics and computational methods to investigate prosopagnosia, rather than addressing any specific sustainable development goals.
applications.quote: We assessed the neural computations in the prosopagnosic patient PS using EEG, RSA, and deep neural networks.

new_primary_category.justification: Since the paper is unrelated to sustainable development, there is no need for proposing a new sustainable development category.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: Given the lack of relevance to sustainable development, proposing a new sub-category in this context is unnecessary.
